summary: dotish@1.0.0 exfiltrates installer.env to attacker Telegram bot on npm install
details: The package's postinstall lifecycle script auto-runs on `npm install` and reads the installer's current working directory `.env` file (typically containing API keys, database credentials, and cloud tokens), then POSTs the full file contents together with `os.hostname()` to a hardcoded Telegram Bot API endpoint. The destination URL is stored as a base64 literal and decoded at runtime to `https://api.telegram.org/bot<redacted>/sendMessage` (bot id 8406833247, chat id 5934680334). Variable names are shaped to obscure the network call, comments are written in Somali, and the outbound request is wrapped in a try/catch that swallows errors. The package presents itself as an env-var utility and does not disclose any of this behavior.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
